_meta.purpose: Frozen synthetic input set for the Story Bank / extract-bullets extraction-quality eval. FROZEN — do not edit inputs between rounds; future rounds score the SAME set so baselines are comparable. Add new inputs only as a versioned append (new id), never by mutating an existing one.
_meta.why_synthetic: The live `stories` table has 0 real-user rows (all 13 are internal), so before/after quality cannot be measured on real data. These inputs are hand-authored to span the real input diversity we expect from business-student pilot users.
diversity_axes: richness: thin (1 clause, no numbers) -> rich (metrics + tools named)
domain: software AND non-software (operations, growth/marketing, business development, analytics)
hygiene: clean prose AND messy realistic paste (typos, run-ons, buried metrics)
_meta.ground_truth_convention: known_metrics / known_tools list the ONLY figures and named tools that actually appear in the input text. The anti-fabrication gate FAILS an output if it emits any number/percentage/currency or named tool that is not groundable in the input text (case/space-insensitive substring, digit-normalised). known_metrics are the verbatim figures the extractor SHOULD carry through when it writes a bullet about them.
_meta.profile_convention: `profile` is the synthetic user context the grounding-context lever injects in --mode grounded (mirrors what the edge fn will fetch from profiles + target roles). It is REFERENCE-ONLY: it may shape skill vocabulary/framing but must NEVER become a source of facts added to a bullet. --mode baseline ignores it.

profile.headline: CS student seeking backend / fintech engineering roles

inputs.text: I wrote a script to clean up our database.
inputs.notes: Skeletal input. Correct behaviour = one honest bullet, no invented metric/tool, no padding. Probes the thin-input floor.

inputs.text: I built a Python fetcher that scored which of our customers were most likely to churn. It cut our false-positive alerts by 40% and ran across all 29 of our Postgres tables. I used SQLAlchemy for the queries and deployed it on a nightly cron.
inputs.notes: Rich input. Correct behaviour = metrics 40% and 29 carried verbatim, tools surfaced. Probes fidelity ceiling.

profile.headline: Operations coordinator moving into ops / program management

inputs.text: I reorganised how we handled inbound shipments — built a new intake process and trained the warehouse team on it. Things moved faster after that.
inputs.notes: Non-software, action + vague outcome, no numbers. Correct behaviour = concrete action+outcome bullet with NO invented number ('faster' must NOT become a %).

inputs.text: I ran our Black Friday email campaign. I segmented the list into 5 cohorts in Klaviyo, wrote all the copy, and we hit a 32% open rate and $48K in attributed revenue, up from $30K the year before.
inputs.notes: Non-software rich. Probes fidelity on a marketing profile + currency-figure handling ($48K/$30K verbatim).

inputs.text: so basically i was doing outbound for the israeli market, cold emails + linkedin, i think i booked like 20 something meetings in q3 and 3 of them closed?? one was a big one ~15k arr... also helped set up the crm stuff in hubspot cuz it was a mess
inputs.notes: Messy realistic paste: typos, lowercase, run-on, hedges ('like 20 something', '~15k'), buried metrics. Probes whether the extractor recovers real figures from noise WITHOUT sharpening a hedge into false precision ('20 something' must not become an exact 20; '~15k arr' stays approximate).

inputs.text: עבדתי על ניתוח נתונים של churn, בניתי dashboard ב-Tableau שהראה למנהלים איפה אנחנו מאבדים לקוחות. הורדנו את ה-churn ב-12% תוך רבעון.
inputs.notes: Hebrew/English mixed (EN: 'I analysed churn data, built a Tableau dashboard showing managers where we lose customers. We reduced churn 12% within a quarter'). Probes the known gpt-4o-mini Hebrew-emission weakness (hebrew-skill-extraction-model-finding: ~5% Hebrew skill emission) AND output-language behaviour — does the bullet come back in English (CV language) or Hebrew? Feeds the held model-tier decision.
